title: An approach combining bioinformatics and machine learning to identify eight autophagy-related biomarkers and construct molecular mechanisms underlying COVID-19 and major depressive disorders.
authors: Yu, C; Zhang, F-J; Zhang, L-L; Xian, D-X; Li, Y; Li, J-J; Tang, S-X; Li, X-J; Liu, Y; Peng, M; Zhang, L; Wang, S
journal: European review for medical and pharmacological sciences
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过生物信息学与机器学习筛选COVID-19合并抑郁症的自噬相关诊断标志物并构建TF-基因调控网络，但核心是疾病标志物与基因调控，缺乏蛋白质-DNA三维互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: OBJECTIVE: A lack of objective biomarkers is preventing the screening and diagnosis of COVID-19 combined with major depression disorder (COVID-19-MDD). The purpose of this study was to identify diagnostic biomarkers and gene regulatory mechanisms associated with autophagy; a crucial process significantly involved in the pathogenesis of COVID-19-MDD. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this study, differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were screened using GSE98793 from the GEO2R analysis (GEO) database, and intersected with the COVID-19-related gene (CRGs) and autophagy-related genes (ARGs) to obtain common genes involved in. Then, Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses of these common genes were performed. Subsequently, the transcription factor (TF)-gene regulatory network and comorbidity network were constructed. In addition, 10 drug candidates were screened using the DSigDB database. To identify diagnostic markers, we used LASSO regression. RESULTS: In total, 13 common genes were screened, which were primarily enriched in lysosomes, endoplasmic reticulum membranes, and other endomembrane systems also associated with autophagy. Additionally, these genes were involved in neurological cell signaling and have a functional role in pathways related to vascular endothelial growth factor, tyrosine kinase, autophagy, inflammation, immunity, and carcinogenesis. Tumors and psychiatric disorders were the most highly linked diseases to COVID-19. Finally, ten drug candidates and eight diagnostic markers (STX17, NRG1, RRAGD, XPO1, HERC1, HSP90AB1, EPHB2, and S1PR3) were screened. CONCLUSIONS: This is the first study to screen eight diagnostic markers and construct a gene regulatory network for COVID-19-MDD from the perspective of autophagy. The findings of our study provide novel insights into the diagnosis and treatment of COVID-19-MDD.
abstract_zh: 目的：缺乏客观生物标志物阻碍了COVID-19合并重度抑郁症（COVID-19-MDD）的筛查和诊断。本研究旨在识别与自噬相关的诊断性生物标志物及基因调控机制；自噬是COVID-19-MDD发病机制中涉及的关键过程。材料与方法：在本研究中，使用GEO2R分析（GEO）数据库中的GSE98793筛选差异表达基因（DEGs），并与COVID-19相关基因（CRGs）和自噬相关基因（ARGs）取交集，以获得涉及的共同基因。随后，对这些共同基因进行基因本体论（GO）和京都基因与基因组百科全书（KEGG）富集分析。接着，构建了转录因子（TF）-基因调控网络和共病网络。此外，使用DSigDB数据库筛选出10种候选药物。为识别诊断标志物，我们采用LASSO回归。结果：共筛选出13个共同基因，这些基因主要富集于溶酶体、内质网膜及其他内膜系统，并与自噬相关。此外，这些基因参与神经细胞信号传导，并在与血管内皮生长因子、酪氨酸激酶、自噬、炎症、免疫和致癌作用相关的通路中发挥功能作用。肿瘤和精神疾病是与COVID-19关联最密切的疾病。最后，筛选出10种候选药物和8个诊断标志物（STX17、NRG1、RRAGD、XPO1、HERC1、HSP90AB1、EPHB2和S1PR3）。结论：这是首次从自噬角度筛选出8个诊断标志物并构建COVID-19-MDD基因调控网络的研究。我们的研究结果为COVID-19-MDD的诊断和治疗提供了新的见解。
